name: code-editor
purpose: Use CodeEditor only when the person edits the code (its diff mode is for editing one side beside the original); to show code, config or JSON the person reads or copies, including read-only diffs, use CodeBlock, and for build, deploy or runtime log lines use LogViewer. An editable code surface with line numbers, diagnostics and a read-only and a diff mode. It is a plain-text editor first: a monospace textarea with a line-number gutter that works on the server, without JavaScript and on any device. When the app passes a `loader` (a function that wires Monaco's workers and returns `import('monaco-editor')`), Monaco is loaded lazily, painted with the design tokens and takes over the same value, markers and options; until it loads, or if it fails, the plain editor stays in place. It differs from `code-block`, which only shows code.
useWhen: Editing a function, a script, a SQL query, a JSON or YAML document inside the product.
Editing code beside the version it changes (diff mode): the saved version stays on the left, read-only, and the edit happens on the right, for example a function changed before a deploy.
Code that the server validates: the diagnostics come back as `markers` and show on their lines and in a list.
A JSON document with a known shape (a function's argument schema, a configuration file): pass its JSON Schema as `schema` and Monaco checks the document against it as the user types.
A read-only view of code that still needs the editor's navigation (find, folding) once Monaco is loaded.
avoidWhen: Showing a snippet to copy, with tabs and a file name → use `code-block`.

Showing a read-only change between two versions (what a release or a revert changes, a configuration before and after) → use `code-block` with the tab's `original`; diff mode is for editing beside the original, not for reviewing a change nobody edits.
A one-line value such as a header, a regex or a path → use `input` inside a `field`.
Free prose or a description → use `textarea`.
A stream of log lines → use `log-viewer`.
A form generated from a JSON schema → use `schema-form` (the arguments tab of a function pairs both).

In a docs Markdown page or the site's page JSON. CodeEditor is app-only (decision RV-C2-1, rule `azion-ui-content-channels`): the person edits code in it, so it has no `DocMarkdown` tag and no page JSON entry. A docs page shows code as a code fence (`DocCodeGroup`); the site uses `CodeBlock`.
related: `code-block` — read-only snippets with copy; same syntax colour tokens.
`textarea` — plain multi-line text; the fallback editor is built in its spirit but keeps code typography and a gutter.
`field` — wraps the editor with a label, a description and an error; the editor reads id, `aria-describedby`, invalid and disabled from it.
`toggle-group` — the document switch (Code / Arguments) placed in the `toolbar` slot.
`log-viewer` — output of a run next to the editor.
bestPractices: Wrap it in a `Field` with a visible label, or give it an `ariaLabel`; the label names the textarea and the Monaco editor.

Pass `loader` from the app so Monaco is code-split and never part of the Azion UI bundle. The loader sets `MonacoEnvironment.getWorker` before it returns `import('monaco-editor')`; without workers Monaco has no language services. With `monaco-editor` 0.56 and later under Vite the worker imports are `monaco-editor/editor/editor.worker?worker` and `monaco-editor/languages/features/<json|css|html|typescript>/<name>.worker?worker` (`ts.worker` serves `javascript` too); the old `monaco-editor/esm/vs/...?worker` paths fail the build. Copy `loadMonaco` from the Usage block or the `Monaco` example.
Set `padLineNumbers` on a full-page code editor (`fill`, a function's Code or Arguments document), as the console does (01, 02…); leave it off on a small editor inside a form.
Function calls are coloured for you (JavaScript and TypeScript, with `--code-syntax-function`); do not register your own Monarch grammar for that.
Send server diagnostics as `markers` with 1-based lines; keep each message one sentence.
Pass a JSON Schema as `schema` for a JSON document with a known shape, and listen to `markers-change` to show the first problem in a `Field.Error`; keep `markers` for what only the server knows.
Set `:bordered="false"` when the editor fills a pane that already frames it (a resizable pane, a full-page function editor, a drawer body); keep the default frame inside a form.
Give the editor a fixed `height`, or `fill` inside a flex column that has its own height; never let it grow with the content.
Use `readonly` for code the user may read and select but not change; use `disabled` only when the whole form is locked.

In diff mode, `original` is the left side and `v-model` the right side, which stays editable. A diff nobody edits is a `code-block` with `original`, which marks every added and removed line without loading an editor.

props.name: language
props.doc: Monaco language id (`javascript`, `typescript`, `json`, `sql`, `lua`, `yaml`…). The fallback ignores it.

props.name: loader
props.doc: Loads Monaco lazily; without it the plain editor is the editor.

props.name: readonly
props.doc: The code can be read, selected and copied but not changed.

props.name: disabled
props.doc: Locks the editor; it leaves the tab order.

props.name: invalid
props.doc: Paints the danger border; also set by a surrounding `Field`.

props.name: diff
props.doc: Shows `original` beside the value as a side-by-side diff.

props.name: original
props.doc: The left side of the diff.

props.name: markers
props.doc: Diagnostics shown on their lines and in the problems list.

props.name: height
props.doc: CSS height of the editing area.

props.name: fill
props.doc: Fills a flex column instead of using `height`.

props.name: bordered
props.doc: Draws the frame: border, corner radius and an offset focus ring. Off, the editor sits flush in its pane.

props.name: padLineNumbers
props.doc: Zero-pads line numbers to two digits (01, 02…), as the console's full-page function and arguments editors do.

props.name: path
props.doc: Model path for Monaco language services (`index.ts`, `args.json`).

props.name: schema
props.doc: JSON Schema the value is checked against when `language` is `json` and Monaco is loaded.

props.name: ariaLabel
props.doc: Accessible name when no `Field` label names it. Empty uses the locale catalog.

events.name: ready
events.notes: Monaco mounted; the payload is the editor instance (for actions).

events.name: load-error
events.notes: The loader rejected; the plain editor stays.

events.name: markers-change
events.notes: The diagnostics Monaco's language services (JSON syntax and `schema`, TypeScript) put on the value, as markers sorted by line, each time they change. The `markers` prop is not echoed back; the plain editor never fires it.

slots.name: toolbar
slots.notes: A bar above the editing area: a document switch, the file name, a Format or Run action.
